subject: Post-demo: role map, decision path, and legal timeline for FinLytics
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Ellis Travers <ellis.travers@finlytics.com>
Cc: Riley Cho <riley.cho@finlytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: FinLytics demo — decision criteria & next steps

Hi Ellis (and team),

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and a suggested next-steps checklist so we can lock the path to procurement.

Key points from the demo
- Primary business driver: accelerate model-driven document classification and reduce manual labeling by 70% over 6 months.
- Performance needs: p95 latency under 300ms for inference flows; batch embedding throughput for nightly jobs.
- Security: data residency for EU-sourced accounts and detailed access control for PII are musts.

Stakeholder map (as we understood it)
- Economic buyer: Ellis Travers (VP Data & Analytics) — owns ROI and budget approval.
- Security: Riley Cho — evaluating SOC2, encryption, and network controls.
- Procurement: procurement@finlytics.com — will own PO and contract milestone approvals.
- Implementation/CS: TBD on your side, but we expect a technical lead during the POC.

Proposed next steps (by priority)
1) Security deep-dive call (45 min) — technical controls, evidence, and architecture diagram. Proposed window: Wed Apr 21 10:00 AM PT.
2) Share draft POC SOW and MAAP checklist (attached) for procurement and legal review.
3) Contract redline cycle: target to complete initial redline by Apr 23 so procurement can route for approvals.
4) Pilot kickoff: aim to start first week of May after sign-off.

Attachments: Redwood-POC-SOW-v1.docx, FinLytics-MAAP-Checklist.pdf (see attachments).

Please confirm: 1) that the stakeholder mapping above is accurate, and 2) availability for the security deep-dive on Apr 21 at 10 AM PT. If those times don't work, propose 2 alternatives.

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | (415) 555-0172

From: Riley Cho <riley.cho@finlytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellis Travers <ellis.travers@finlytics.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@finlytics.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: FinLytics demo — decision criteria & next steps

Ben,

Appreciate the clear recap. A few items from security's side before we schedule the deep-dive:
- Evidence: We need a SOC2 Type II report (most recent), pen-test summary, and details on key management (KMS/HSM) options.
- Data handling: Clarify whether inference can be restricted to our VPC or if tokens leave our environment for any hosted flows.
- Encryption: At-rest AES-256 and TLS 1.2+ in transit required. Please confirm key rotation policy.
- Compliance: Any third-party subprocessors must be listed for the audit.

Procurement timeline note: We are targeting an internal approval decision by the end of Q2, but legal review typically needs 7-10 business days after initial redline. Procurement will open a PO only after a legal-signed contract.

Can you provide an architecture diagram and a short security questionnaire (one-pager) ahead of the deep-dive? That will speed the review. Also, include contacts for your Contracts and Security leads so I can loop them in.

Riley
Security Lead, FinLytics
riley.cho@finlytics.com | +1 617-555-3310

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Ellis Travers <ellis.travers@finlytics.com>, Riley Cho <riley.cho@finlytics.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: FinLytics demo — decision criteria & next steps

Thanks Riley — quick answers and an concrete proposal to keep momentum.

Immediate answers
- SOC2: we will share our latest SOC2 Type II report and pen-test summary prior to the deep-dive.
- VPC: Redwood supports private deployment options. For the hosted flows we offer VPC peering and private endpoints; tokens do not persist beyond inference unless customer opts-in for logging.
- Encryption: AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit, and we support KMS integration with customer-managed keys. Key rotation policies documented in our security packet.
- Subprocessors: list attached in the MAAP checklist.

Decision criteria (mapped to owners)
- Cost: total cost of ownership and per-token economics — Ellis (economic buyer).
- Latency & availability: p95 latency <300ms and 99.9% SLA — Engineering/Infra lead (will confirm name).
- Security/compliance: SOC2, VPC/HSM options, subprocessors — Riley (security).
- Contracting: indemnities, data residency clauses, termination for convenience — Procurement & Legal.

Proposed owners & deadlines
- Security deep-dive (45 min) with Redwood Security: Wed Apr 21 10:00 AM PT — owners: Riley + Redwood security lead (I can introduce).
- Contract redline first pass: Redwood to deliver clean SOW and contract template by Apr 18; FinLytics legal to return first redline by Apr 23.
- Procurement PO path: Procurement to confirm required approval chain by Apr 19.

Action items for this thread
- Ben: share SOC2 + pen-test + architecture diagram + updated SOW (today).
- Marissa: prep two-slide exec summary focusing on ROI and SLA for Ellis.
- Neha: assemble SOC2 evidence set and subprocessors list.

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/FL-2027-042), demo notes (https://drive.google.com/finlytics-demo-notes).

Attachments: Redwood-POC-SOW-v1.docx, FinLytics-MAAP-Checklist.pdf

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
